cands.name: Abe Jones
cands.bio: Abraham P. Jones is a Democrat who has represented North Carolina House District 38 (Wake County) since 2021. A Harvard Law graduate, he has been a federal law clerk, assistant U.S. attorney, assistant attorney general, administrative law judge and Superior Court judge. He served on the Wake County Board of Commissioners from 1990 to 1994.
cands.gaps: We found no documented actions or stated positions by Abe Jones on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, police pay, gun laws, abortion or school choice. His campaign site covers affordable housing, vocational education and criminal justice reform in general terms, but the pages we read gave no specific commitments. He did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in any recent cycle. We found no news reports of controversies and no notable endorsements; Ballotpedia lists only two online voter-guide groups for 2026. His 2012 defeat for re-election as a judge and his 2014 and 2016 losses in Court of Appeals races are on record, but nothing we read suggests misconduct. We could not confirm his county commissioner service from a primary source.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born in Wilson, NC, and his campaign site says he grew up in Raleigh and attended Wake County public schools, so he was born and raised in North Carolina.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2021 and on the Wake County Board of Commissioners (1990-94). He was a Superior Court judge for 17 years (1995-2012), and earlier an assistant U.S. attorney, NC assistant attorney general, administrative law judge, private practitioner and law firm owner. He has also taught at UNC School of Law.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service and local elected office, plus a nearly 40-year law career, which fits the high band for writing law and the state budget. Committee assignments were not counted.
